papers.title: Noether's Second Theorem and the Pareto Front Structure in Multi-Criteria Variational Problems
papers.abstract: This paper establishes a rigorous connection between Noether's second theorem and the structure of Pareto fronts in multi-criteria variational problems. We prove that for a family of functionals invariant under a common gauge Lie group, the regular part of the Pareto front is contained in the union of solutions to weighted Euler--Lagrange equations, and that on Pareto-optimal sections, combinations of Noether currents are conserved. Gauge symmetries are shown to impose additional constraints on the Lagrange multipliers via Bianchi-type identities, reducing the dimension of the admissible weight space. Two practical approaches are derived from this result: dimensionality reduction via gauge fixing and scalarization with penalty terms. The theory is validated on three classical problems: the linear-quadratic regulator with two criteria, a model predictive control problem with a minimax criterion, and the double integrator with control constraints. In each case, the Pareto front is shown to satisfy an exact conservation law, and the analytical structure of the front is recovered from the symmetries of the problem. The results demonstrate that gauge functions (null Lagrangians) can restore invariants even when the dynamics break the symmetry, and that control constraints do not destroy the underlying conservation laws but merely restrict the admissible set. The proposed approach yields a Pareto front with minimal deviation from the theoretical curve, outperforming known multi-objective algorithms, and provides a new foundation for the analytical treatment of multi-criteria optimization in nonlinear dynamics and control.
authors: Evgeny Nikulchev

papers.title: Physical regimes of quartic quantum advantage in elastic media simulation
papers.abstract: Quantum algorithms for elastic media simulation have been conjectured to offer up to a quartic quantum advantage over classical methods; however, the devil is always in the details. Here, we determine key physical conditions under which this quartic separation could be achieved in the relevant parameters. For continuum elastic dynamics at fixed volume with spatial convergence order $m$, we find that the end-to-end speedup is of order $(m+4)/(m+1)$ in the simulation time, and $4/(m+1)$ in the accuracy, with exponential memory advantage. For elastic lattice systems, we define microscopically resolved bulk observables (MRBOs) as those that can be efficiently extracted from a quantum state, but cannot be resolved by a known continuum model with fewer degrees of freedom than the lattice. We then argue that the estimation of MRBOs is a candidate problem for quartic quantum advantage in problem size. We propose MRBOs for pseudorandom heterogeneous materials as an explicit end-to-end application where this occurs, while admitting efficient `quantum cheese' encodings of the material properties. We thus demonstrate how the interplay between regularity, physical scale, observable sensitivity and quantum encodability constrains the relation between classical and quantum complexity.
authors: David Jennings, Kamil Korzekwa, Matteo Lostaglio, Tam\'as Vaszary

papers.title: FNO-Based Inverse Co-Design of Semiconducting Quantum-Dot Devices
papers.abstract: Gate-defined semiconductor quantum dots are promising building blocks for scalable spin-based quantum processors, however their operational properties depend on several fabrication and control parameters, such as lithographic gate layout and applied voltages. Existing device architectures have been refined through repeated fabrication and experimental testing, producing layouts that support reliable device operation. However, this process does not exhaustively explore the design space, limiting the ability to obtain qubits with targeted properties. We address these challenges by presenting a differentiable inverse co-design framework for electrostatically defined quantum dots that jointly optimises gate voltages and the gate electrode layout. A semiclassical Thomas--Fermi electrostatic simulator provides reference data for a Fourier neural operator (FNO) surrogate, which predicts the two-dimensional charge-density field. The desired spatial distribution of the confined charge defines the target quantum-dot geometry for inverse design. The FNO reproduces charge densities with a relative $L^2$ test error of just 0.6\% and enables millisecond-scale differentiable evaluations. Relative to the CPU-based physics simulator, the FNO achieves a 17,000-fold speed-up on GPU for a single design, with further performance gains enabled by batched inference. When embedded in a gradient-based design loop with fabrication constraints, the FNO can produce both vertically and horizontally elongated double-dot confinement geometries from the same initial conditions. The ability to engineer these distinct confinement configurations demonstrates control over quantum-dot shape and position, providing a route towards designing devices with distinct qubit-relevant operating properties prior to fabrication.
authors: Marek Rychetsky, Valentin Duruisseaux, Freya Shah, David L. Craig, Ming Ni, Georgios Katsaros, Taylor L. Patti, Anima Anandkumar, Natalia Ares

papers.title: All Bell inequalities with a quantum advantage in the minimal scenario are self-testing
papers.abstract: In the minimal Bell scenario, all extremal quantum correlations are known, but the Tsirelson inequalities that delimit the quantum set remain poorly understood. We study which correlations can maximize a given Tsirelson inequality, and conversely, which inequalities are maximized by a given correlation. We show that every Tsirelson inequality with quantum advantage is maximized by a single, extremal correlation, and thus self-tests the corresponding realization. This characterizes all self-tests based on linear Bell inequalities in this scenario. We also show that at most a two-dimensional family of inequalities can be maximized by a nonlocal extremal correlation. We identify these as polygons for a family of correlations realized by qubit states of arbitrary entanglement. This allows us to deduce that the quantum set is not self-dual.
authors: Mu-En Liu, Andrea Zingarofalo, Victor Barizien, Jean-Daniel Bancal

papers.title: Matrix Theory from Holography II: Beyond Counting
papers.abstract: Extending our earlier realization of Matrix Theory for M-theory within AdS/CFT, we propose and test a new triality among a large-charge sector of three-dimensional $\mathcal N=4$ ADHM theory, the BMN matrix model, and lightlike-compactified M-theory on the maximally supersymmetric pp-wave. In an appropriate triple-scaling limit, the superconformal index of ADHM theory becomes the grand-canonical index of the BMN model, with magnetic-flux sectors corresponding to fuzzy-sphere vacua. But the real interest of this new setup is that we can go beyond counting states. Using supersymmetric localization, we show that correlation functions in topological subsectors agree as well, including their nontrivial dependence on the BMN coupling. In each magnetic-flux sector, both the localization measure and the operator insertions can be matched precisely with those of the corresponding BMN vacuum. Our results also point to a deeper connection between monopole bubbling in ADHM theory and instantons in the BMN model. For minuscule monopole charges, ADHM correlators map directly to topological correlators in the trivial BMN vacuum. For non-minuscule charges, monopole bubbling produces additional screened sectors, whose relative weights reproduce the classical actions of BMN instantons. Mirror symmetry offers another perspective on this structure, mapping the monopole operators to Higgs-branch ``winding" operators in the mirror necklace theory. Finally, we discuss a type IIB counterpart, connecting a large-charge sector of four-dimensional $\mathbb Z_K$-orbifold quiver theories, the DLCQ of type IIB string theory on the pp-wave, and level-one mass-deformed ABJM theory on $\mathbb R_t\times T^2$. As a first test, we show that the superconformal index of the orbifold theory reproduces the vacuum degeneracy of the mass-deformed ABJM theory.
authors: Shota Komatsu, Eunwoo Lee, Chintan Patel

papers.title: Multipartite Entanglement, TQFT Partition Functions and PL Bordism
papers.abstract: In a previous work we conjectured that the multi-invariants of the ground state of a gapped $(d-1)+1$-dimensional system, labeled by bipartite $(d+1)$-edge-colored graphs encoding closed oriented $d$-manifolds $M$, compute the partition functions $Z(M)$ of the low energy topological quantum field theory (TQFT), up to non-universal factors determined by the local structure of the triangulation. In this paper we determine which combinations of partition functions can be isolated from the non-universal factors. The answer is governed by oriented bordism. If $M$ is null-bordant, $Z(M)$ is obtained from an explicit, state-independent finite family of multi-invariants, up to a power of $Z(S^d)$ which is fixed to be $Z(S^d)^{\chi(M)/2}$ for even $d$ and can be removed for odd $d$. Conversely, the obstruction is measured by a quotient of the group of "residues" of colored graphs which receives a surjective map from the oriented bordism group, with kernel precisely the torsion subgroup as far as smooth manifolds are concerned. In $d=4$ the obstruction is the signature: $Z(M)/Z(S^4)^{\chi(M)/2}$ can be extracted if and only if $\sigma(M)=0$. This is due to the fact that the first Pontryagin class $p_1$ has a local expression and thus $e^{i\theta\sigma(M)}=e^{\frac{i}{3}\theta\int_M p_1}$ cannot be separated from the non-universal factors. Torsion invariants, in contrast, are not obstructed: for the ground state of the $4+1$-dimensional invertible phase with partition function $(-1)^{\int w_2w_3}$ we compute the multi-invariants exactly, and two graphs with identical local data, encoding the Dold manifold and $\mathbb{CP}^2\times S^1$, give opposite signs.
authors: Michele Del Zotto, Abhijit Gadde, Pavel Putrov

papers.title: Fermion$\text{-}$Monopole Scattering: A Unified Perspective
papers.abstract: We revisit the scattering of massless chiral fermions by a minimally charged BPS 't Hooft-Polyakov monopole. Existing proposals emphasize different aspects of this process and their connections are often unclear, giving rise to apparent conflicts concerning the outgoing states, energy conservation, and anomalous scattering amplitudes. We clarify the connection between different proposals within a common low-energy fermion-rotor description. Starting from the monopole background, we derive the rotor coupling and retain explicit fermion operators throughout the analysis. By adjoining a decoupled auxiliary scalar, we construct a dual theory that permits exact quantization. We show that the rotor vertex has a continuous spectral support down to zero energy and that its infrared exchange relations identify it as the twist dressing of the outgoing fermion. We also compute anomalous fermion correlators directly from fermion zero modes generated by winding configurations of the compact rotor. These results connect rotor dynamics, twisted outgoing states, and the zero-mode origin of anomalous correlators, resolving apparent conflicts and showing how the existing proposals fit into a mutually consistent picture within their common regime of applicability.
authors: Hao Geng, Zekai Wang

papers.title: Asymptotic safety is not generic
papers.abstract: Asymptotically safe quantum gravity proposes a non-perturbative ultraviolet completion of gravity in which the high-energy behavior is controlled by an ultraviolet fixed point---the Reuter fixed point---for which there is robust evidence from a wide range of settings and truncations. The existence of asymptotic safety requires non-trivial zeros of beta functions, raising the question of how generic such fixed-point solutions are. In this work, we tackle this issue by investigating chiral perturbation theories. We focus on SU(2) and SU(3) chiral models, which share key features with gravity such as perturbative non-renormalizability or nonlinear interactions, but which are known to admit a different ultraviolet completion via new degrees of freedom. Using the functional renormalization group, we study these theories within a quartic-derivative truncation and find no evidence for an interacting fixed point. This result suggests that asymptotic safety is not generic, but rather a feature pertaining to certain special systems.
authors: Francesco Del Porro, Francesco Ferrarin, Alessia Platania

papers.title: Nonlocal magic of fermions is bounded by entanglement fluctuations and is logarithmic for free fermions
papers.abstract: Free-fermion states are classically simulable, yet, written as qubits, they typically carry extensive magic, the quantum resource that stabilizer circuits lack. Part of this magic is nonlocal: local unitaries acting separately on two parts of the system cannot remove it. If these local unitaries are restricted to Gaussian ones, the nonlocal magic grows linearly with the number $m$ of partially entangled fermion pairs. We show that this growth is an artifact of the Gaussian restriction: local Gaussian unitaries minimize the nonlocal stabilizer R\'enyi entropy for up to three pairs, but not from four pairs on. General local non-Gaussian unitaries that respect fermion parity take $m$ free-fermion pairs to fermionic Bell pairs with a fidelity that decays at most as $1/\sqrt m$ compared to exponential decay with Gaussian unitaries, so the nonlocal magic drops from linear to logarithmic in $m$. The reason is statistical --- Bell pairs have equal Schmidt weights, that is, a fully degenerate entanglement spectrum, and a state can stay far from them only if its Schmidt weights are spread over many orders of magnitude. This spread is measured by the capacity of entanglement $C_E$, the variance of the entanglement Hamiltonian, and the nonlocal magic of any fermionic state grows at most logarithmically with $C_E$. Free-fermion pairs add to $C_E$ independently, so $C_E$ grows only linearly in $m$, and this leads to the stabilizer fidelity decreasing at most as $1/\sqrt m$. Almost all the magic of free fermions, including Hartree--Fock and BCS mean-field states, is therefore local.
authors: Raghav G. Jha, Dengyao Luo, Alexander F. Kemper, Bojko N. Bakalov

papers.title: Conformal Bootstrap Unblocked
papers.abstract: We develop a novel conformal bootstrap formulated directly in terms of conformal symmetry, reflection positivity, and crossing symmetry, without explicitly relying on the operator product expansion or conformal blocks. By constructing Gram matrices from states created by pairs of local operators and imposing spectral constraints through conformal generators, we obtain a hierarchy of semidefinite programs that directly constrain correlation functions. We demonstrate the method in one to three dimensions, obtaining correlator and spectral bounds that capture generalized free field behavior and reproduce the characteristic Ising kinks in two and three dimensions. We further show that joint positivity of states at different insertion configurations naturally constrains correlators away from self-dual kinematics.
authors: Li-Yuan Chiang, David Poland

papers.title: To Infinity and Beyond: Maximizing Entanglement and Emergent Symmetries in $N$ Higgs Doublet Models
papers.abstract: In this paper, we explore the recent observation that maximizing flavor entanglement in Higgs boson scattering in a two Higgs doublet model leads to parameter space where the potential, if bounded from below, has an enhanced mirror symmetry $U(2)^2$. Looking at $N$ Higgs doublet models, we find a generalization of the mirror models, with $U(2)^N$ symmetry. Focusing on three Higgs doublet models, we determine that there is also a bounded potential solution that maximally entangles but has only the minimal $U(2)$ symmetry. This counterexample demonstrates that additional constraints must be imposed to maintain the connection between maximal entanglement and extended symmetries. As a potential constraint, for the three Higgs doublet model, we show that requiring maximal entanglement still occurs after gauging the symmetries eliminates the counterexample, thus restoring the connection.
authors: Spencer Chang, Gabriel Jacobo

papers.title: Critical collapse remains discretely self-similar at large D
papers.abstract: When matter collapses at the threshold of black hole formation spacetime typically has an emergent continuous or discrete symmetry, depending on the matter content. For the Einstein-Klein-Gordon model in any finite dimension D>3 the associated critical spacetime solutions exhibit discrete self-similarity, characterized by the echoing period Delta. Combining analytical and numerical results with dimensions up to D=200 we predict Delta remains finite at infinite dimension D, contrary to a recent conjecture. We find the fit Delta=1.6439+10.37/D-O(1/D^2) and provide an explicit large-D model.
authors: Christian Ecker, Florian Ecker, Daniel Grumiller

papers.title: On Entanglement Dynamics in Holographic Theories
papers.abstract: Entanglement entropy (EE) is central to modern theoretical physics, yet its calculation in interacting theories with nontrivial time dependence remains challenging. In this thesis, we investigate the real-time dynamics of EE in strongly coupled quantum field theories (QFTs) using the Anti-de Sitter/Conformal Field Theory (AdS/CFT) correspondence. We first examine EE evolution in an exactly solvable two-dimensional conformal field theory (CFT) with an inhomogeneous sine-square deformation (SSD). We argue that the unconventional time evolution driven by the SSD Hamiltonian can be viewed as a change in spacetime foliation, producing new horizons in the dual three-dimensional bulk. Holographic EE calculations agree with CFT results in all comparable cases. We then study entanglement dynamics in generic chaotic quantum many-body systems. In the limit of late time and large regions, these dynamics are believed to admit an effective entanglement membrane description. In 2d CFTs, a degenerate membrane tension reproduces several entropy dynamics results, unlike the non-degenerate tension in higher dimensions. Using holography, we show that capturing reflected entropy in 2d CFT requires an additional degree of freedom in the membrane description. We further show that a conventional non-degenerate tension emerges when the CFT undergoes a relevant deformation, holographically dual to a planar Banados-Teitelboim-Zanelli (BTZ) black hole with scalar hair and an interior Kasner universe. We then develop a membrane effective theory for reflected entropy dynamics in higher dimensions. Finally, we apply the membrane theories for reflected entropy to study the time evolution of multipartite entanglement signals. We found that scrambling dynamics generate multipartite entanglement with rich structures.
authors: Hanzhi Jiang

papers.title: Constraining the spectral gap of 2d CFTs just above c=1
papers.abstract: We numerically study the space of compact unitary two-dimensional conformal field theories (2d CFTs) with central charge $c>1$ using the modular bootstrap. We focus on bounding the spectral gap $\Delta_{\rm gap}$ of such theories, namely the smallest scaling dimension among the non-vacuum primary operators. We use both a primal method that directly searches for consistent spectra and a dual method that yields rigorous exclusions. A key feature of our analysis is requiring the degeneracies of primary operators to be positive integers. At $c$ very near $1$, the integrality constraint greatly reduces the allowed spectral gap in both methods. For example, at $c-1 = 3\times 10^{-3}$ integrality strengthens the rigorous bound from $\Delta_{\rm gap} \lesssim 0.5$ to $\Delta_{\rm gap} < 0.041$. Our results suggest that the spectral gap might vanish as $c$ approaches $1$ from above.
authors: Nathan Benjamin, Kevin Langhoff, Wei Li, Jesse Thaler

papers.title: Chern-Simons Interfaces and Minimal Models from Quantum Groups
papers.abstract: Coupling two-dimensional fundamental Dirac fermions to $SU(N)_k$ Chern-Simons theory produces non-chiral interfaces that in the infrared flow to a compact boson and a $W_N$ minimal model. We propose a description of these interfaces as continuum limits of $q$-deformed fermion chains. The $q$-deformation is achieved by coupling a chain of one-dimensional fundamental complex fermions to $SU(N)_k$ Chern-Simons theory, keeping the underlying topological gauge field continuous. The operator algebra is controlled by quantum groups, which provide an algebraic perspective on the usual categorical formulation of anyon chains. As an application, we derive a Lieb-Schultz-Mattis constraint involving baryon-number and lattice translation, obstructing a unique symmetric gapped ground state. At unit filling, we gap out the compact boson sector with a Mott term and obtain standard anyon chain Hamiltonians previously studied in the literature. This provides an anomaly argument for the existence of $N$ copies of minimal model sectors permuted by lattice translation in the infrared.
authors: Suriyah Rajalingam Kannagi, Sergio Sanjurjo

papers.title: Constraint Variance Identity and the Matter-Geometry Fluctuation Relation
papers.abstract: The quantum Hamiltonian constraint vanishes for physical states. For separable Hamiltonians in minisuperspace, its vanishing variance yields a fundamental identity. Under the Born-Oppenheimer approximation, we derive the Matter-Geometry Fluctuation Relation, dynamically linking spacetime clock fluctuations to matter fluctuations. This establishes a quantitative stability condition for the clock against total quantum noise. Finally, we obtain an uncertainty relation between matter energy and relational time. The stable existence of spacetime thus demands quantum fluctuations in matter.
authors: Yuki Yokokura

papers.title: Running Couplings in CP Violating Abelian Theories
papers.abstract: We calculate the one- and two-loop running couplings for a massless photon coupled to dyons, including CP violating couplings. The electric and magnetic source vertices in the most general theory form a real coupling matrix $C$, while a current-current interaction depends on $C^T C$ and the quantized determinant $\det C$. These determine, respectively, the continuously running Coulombic interactions and the fixed antisymmetric Dirac--Schwinger--Zwanziger charge quantization condition which also determines pairwise helicity. The running preserves $\det C$, showing that the electric and magnetic couplings run inversely while every pairwise helicity remains constant. We comment on how the running of the CP-odd coupling $\theta$ relates to physical CP violation, which also depends on the spectrum, mass phases, and threshold corrections. We also show that an invertible field redefinition moves the CP-odd coupling between the current source terms and the photon kinetic terms; these are two descriptions of the same local interaction. Finally, we show that the result agrees with the Argyres--Douglas $\beta$ function ansatz.
authors: Joshua Newey, John Terning, Christopher B. Verhaaren

papers.title: Threshold-Free Symmetry-Enriched Topological Quantum Memory
papers.abstract: We show that non-Abelian symmetry enrichment can protect a toric code memory against incoherent electric noise at any bond error probability $p\in[0,1]$. For a toric code on the honeycomb lattice coupled to $Sp(N)$ rotors, with electric anyons carrying the fundamental representation, we construct an efficient minimum-weight decoder whose logical error probability decays exponentially with system size for $N\ge40$, a conservative sufficient bound. The same decoder also rules out strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking in the fundamental channel of $Sp(N)$ under the corresponding local decoherence in two dimensions. The construction extends to other symmetries, including $SU(N)$.
authors: Abhijat Sarma, Ruochen Ma, Cenke Xu

papers.title: Charged AdS$_{3}$ black branes as marginally deformed two-dimensional CFTs
papers.abstract: We study how boundary correlation functions encode the charge dependence of the renormalised Euclidean action of an AdS$_3$ black brane. In three-dimensional Einstein-Maxwell theory, the Maxwell field has logarithmic asymptotics and is locally dual to a massless pseudoscalar. In the canonical ensemble, the charge density fixes the slope of a spatially linear source for the dual marginal operator. At fixed temperature, the classical action is even in the charge density due to reflection symmetry $\Phi\to-\Phi$, and its charge expansion coefficients are governed by Catalan numbers. We compute the quadratic and quartic terms from connected correlation functions around the neutral brane. The scalar two-point function and the shift symmetry of its source determine the matter Weyl anomaly, which fixes the logarithmic temperature dependence of the quadratic term in the charge expansion. At quartic order, the connected four-point function comes from tree-level graviton exchange. Integrating it against the linear source, with an infrared cutoff on the overall scale of the integral, reproduces the quartic coefficient of the action per unit length. At each higher order, the corresponding Catalan coefficient predicts the integrated sum of all connected tree-level Witten diagrams.
authors: Suting Zhao, Gabriel Arenas-Henriquez, Yizhou Lu, Hamed Adami, Ren\'e Meyer

papers.title: Single-shot ground-state preparation via strongly coupled baths
papers.abstract: Preparing ground and thermal states of quantum many-body systems is a central task in quantum simulation. Dissipative protocols have emerged as a promising solution for both near-term and fault-tolerant hardware, but most constructions rely on weak system-bath coupling, leading to slow cooling. Here, we construct cooling protocols at strong system-bath coupling, and demonstrate accurate state preparation within even a single cooling cycle. Our protocols combine dynamically ramped ancilla energy levels with time-dependent couplings to optimize the trade-off between cooling error and physical time. For a general class of free-fermion systems, we reduce the dynamics exactly to a two-level scattering problem: ground-state cooling becomes a control problem of maximizing resonant excitation transfer while suppressing non-adiabatic heating. We then construct a family of ``M\"obius-Ingham'' protocols, which reach optimal error scaling for gapless spectra and almost-exponential suppression of the leading heating error for gapped spectra, as a function of the cycle period. In our free-fermion benchmarks, M\"obius-Ingham cooling lies on the Pareto frontier between steady-state error and cooling time among the controls tested. We further demonstrate its effectiveness in interacting Ising and $t$-$V$ chains and the two-dimensional Fermi-Hubbard model. Finally, we extend our construction to Gibbs state preparation, showing how free-fermion thermal states can be prepared in a single cycle.
authors: Liang-Hong Mo, Jerome Lloyd, Yuxuan Zhang, Dmitry A. Abanin, Biao Lian

papers.title: Finite is not enough: Triviality bounds in nonlocal field theories
papers.abstract: An ultraviolet-finite theory need not be ultraviolet complete. This observation weakens the case for spacetime discreteness in quantum gravity if that case rests on removing ultraviolet divergences alone. We arrive at this observation by deriving the one-loop momentum-subtraction flow in four-dimensional $\phi^4$ theories with ultraviolet-suppressing form factors. The suppression freezes the running above the nonlocality scale, but the theory can hit a Landau pole before suppression sets in. We obtain a bound on the infrared coupling by requiring perturbative control at all scales. This bound varies only at the percent level across the examples we consider. We expect similar bounds in models of discrete spacetime. Thus, requiring ultraviolet completeness improves the predictivity of nonlocal theories.
authors: Fabian Wagner

papers.title: Agnostic and efficient detection of $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry-protected topological phases in projected entangled-pair states
papers.abstract: Symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phases are the simplest example of quantum phases that cannot be detected by local order parameters. Their classification is by now well-established from multiple perspectives, a prominent one being via tensor network states. The practical question, however, is not mere classification, but detection: given the ground state of an interacting Hamiltonian and a symmetry group $G$ along with its representation, is there an efficient way to tell if the state is in a SPT phase with respect to $G$? While there exist such practical tests in one spatial dimension (1D), methods in 2D have so far been restricted to finite-size systems or require an explicit form of virtual symmetries of the tensor networks representing the ground state. Here, we develop an agnostic and efficient method to detect interacting $\mathbb{Z}_2$ 2D SPT phases, using an infinite projected entangled-pair (PEPS) representation of the ground state. The method is agnostic to the symmetry representation in the virtual space of the PEPS tensor and applicable independent of the bond dimension of the tensors. Moreover, it is efficient as it does not require finite-size scalings: it works directly in the thermodynamic limit. We numerically demonstrate the procedure by mapping out phase boundaries away from fixed-point wavefunctions. We extract the SPT label cocycle data explicitly from the PEPS tensor.
authors: Alexandre Chaduteau, Hao Chen, Juraj Hasik, Titus Neupert

papers.title: Ground-State Dressing and Delayed Feedback of a Chiral Giant Atom in Ultrastrong Waveguide QED
papers.abstract: We study a chiral giant atom ultrastrongly coupled to a one-dimensional waveguide at two spatially separated points. At a relative coupling phase \pi/2, the total spectral density is independent of the distance between the coupling points, whereas its directional components are not. Using a variational polaron transformation, we show that the renormalized transition frequency and the total ground-state dressing inherit this independence, while the virtual-photon cloud remains chiral. A sudden switch-off of the coupling releases this cloud as directional radiation. We also derive the spontaneous-emission dynamics in the polaron frame, showing that, after neglecting the local photonic potential, the memory kernel becomes distance independent at the same phase.
authors: Giuseppe Musolino, Daniele Lamberto, Salvatore Savasta, Federico Roccati

papers.title: Coherent detector responses to quantum-controlled spherical-shell geometries
papers.abstract: A detector inside a static spherical shell samples globally matched field modes even though its local geometry is flat. We construct the response of a compactly switched Unruh-DeWitt detector on a quantum-controlled pair of transparent spherical-shell spacetimes with common Arnowitt-Deser-Misner mass. A stipulated common-incoming scattering identification places the branch excitations in one Hilbert space. Their positive Gram matrix determines joint, conditional, and dephased detector responses at a finite common readout, retaining the physical detector-clock phase in the uncompensated protocol. An additional coherent phase-gate protocol compensates free detector-clock propagation while preserving the shell interaction response. For concentric shells the centered response is exactly $s$ wave. A common incoming direction basis extends the construction to a lab-fixed detector and displaced shell centers, preserving common-translation covariance. The equal-radius benchmark exhibits conditional changes of order $25\%$ without dark-port amplification. Combining radius and position produces an assignment-odd response that reverses under reflection and vanishes at the relational midpoint. The relative normalized-state contrast reaches $34.15\%$ among the computed samples; the relative clock-resolved probe-influence contrast reaches $8.09\%$ for the declared readout, while larger values belong to its separate shared-phase envelope. These effects already occur in the dominant-energy-condition-compatible core. They are relational, model-dependent detector responses, not a background-independent witness of quantum geometry. First-order coefficients have finite pointlike limits; finite-coupling statements are made only at a fixed shared regulator.
authors: Shoshauna Gauvin, Robert B. Mann

papers.title: The 2d Ising Model on Hyperbolic Lattices and the Role of Boundary Conditions
papers.abstract: We investigate the role of boundary conditions in the critical behaviour of the ferromagnetic Ising model on regular hyperbolic tessellations. Using worm and Metropolis simulations, we compare open boundaries with wired boundaries implemented through a common auxiliary spin. For open boundaries, the susceptibility exhibits volume-based finite-size scaling with non-mean-field scaling exponents that are approximately stable across four tessellations, supporting the possibility of a common universality class. Comparisons with Binder crossings and susceptibility peaks reveal substantial finite-size effects. For wired boundaries, the central-to-auxiliary spin correlator exhibits radial scaling consistent with a mean-field magnetization exponent. The central-spin response to a uniform magnetic field provides a further consistency test of $\delta=3$. Layer-resolved responses to a weak boundary field also reveal an enhancement of the induced magnetization towards the interior. Our results highlight the importance of boundary conditions and the distinction between interior and whole-system observables in characterizing critical phenomena on non-amenable lattices.
authors: Pallabi Dey, Debasish Banerjee, Arnab Kundu, Ritam Sinha

papers.title: Langmuir kinetics and totally asymmetric volume exclusion in linear chains via Fock space formalism
papers.abstract: Driven-diffusive systems combining spatial exclusion and bulk exchange, such as the totally asymmetric simple exclusion process coupled with Langmuir kinetics (TASEP-LK), serve as foundational models for particle transport in vehicular traffic, conveyor networks, and mesoscopic flow channels. In this work, we employ an exact Doi-Peliti field-theoretic operator formulation in Fock space to evaluate steady-state observables, continuous phase landscapes, and spatial correlations in finite linear chains up to $k = 16$. By introducing a decomposition in terms of biorthonormal eigenvectors for asymmetric non-Hermitian matrices, the stationary state is calculated directly from the kernel of the quasi-Hamiltonian, completely bypassing the computationally prohibitive complexity of full matrix diagonalization and time-dependent matrix exponentiation. Across distinct rate regimes and global parametric scans, our exact discrete calculations demonstrate that finite-size stochastic fluctuations naturally smear out singular domain walls, producing smooth density profiles and continuous phase crossovers. Finite-size scaling illustrates how local profiles systematically steepen toward the sharp domain wall predicted by continuum field theory as $k \to \infty$. Furthermore, two-point correlation analysis reveals that in slow-kinetics regimes, spatial fluctuations generate strong inter-site cumulants, causing standard mean-field approximations to systematically underestimate joint occupancy probabilities by 50\%. These findings emphasize the necessity of analytical methods for modeling mesoscopic transport systems and short traffic corridors where local stochastic fluctuations and spatial correlations dominate the stationary dynamics.
authors: Luis D. S. Silva, Arthur M. S. Carvalho, Francisco A. G. Almeida, Gerson C. Duarte-Filho

papers.title: Minimal massive completions of partially broken higher-spin models
papers.abstract: The partially broken Fronsdal (PBF) model describes massless particles of arbitrary integer spin $s$ with a gauge symmetry smaller than Fronsdal's, and differs from it only by the coefficient $c$ of the term $(\p\cdot h')^2$. We ask whether it admits a genuinely new massive completion. Adding a mass term and the most general local auxiliary sector with at most two derivatives, and demanding that all lower-spin sectors be non-dynamical, we show that for $s=3$ a single auxiliary scalar is never enough, while two scalars give a solution unique up to field redefinitions: one scalar is algebraic and its elimination exactly undoes the deformation, while the other is the auxiliary scalar of the Aragone--Deser--Yang (ADY) model. The same mechanism, with an algebraic vector, appears for $s=4$ and extends to arbitrary spin, and we conjecture that the resulting auxiliary content is minimal. In this minimal completion $c$ does not survive the mass: the correlation functions of $h$ coincide with those of the ADY model. For the Skvortsov--Vasiliev (SV) model, which belongs to the same family, we construct a massive version in which the Weyl-like symmetry survives the mass, and show that its auxiliary sector is fixed by the absence of lower-spin modes, within a general ansatz for $s=3$ and within a restricted one for $s=4$. For the partially broken SV model we obtain instead a massive completion which requires no auxiliary field beyond those of the massive SV model, and in which $c$ survives the mass through the same contact term as in the massless theory.
authors: E. L. Mendon\c{c}a, M. I. C. Mau\'es

papers.title: Unruh-DeWitt detectors in a delocalized massive shell
papers.abstract: We construct a model for the response of a detector to vacuum fluctuations inside a massive hollow shell in a superposition of positions. The delocalized source mass gives rise to a superposition of spacetime geometries and their associated vacuum fluctuations. To describe this system, we employ the formalism of quantum reference frames to transition to a frame in which the source mass occupies a definite position while the detector is in a superposition of positions. This allows the dynamics of the detector to be analyzed using standard tools of quantum field theory on a definite curved spacetime. We compute the detector response for a wide range of configurations of the shell and detector positions and investigate how information about the quantum state of the shell is encoded in the response function, identifying features of the superposition that are effectively captured by the detector. In particular, we show that, under appropriate postselection, the response function exhibits interference patterns, and identify regions of the parameter space of the model in which the shell-induced contributions to the interference terms are maximized.
authors: Giovanna F. do Valle, Saadat Salman Shariff, Nat\'alia S. M\"oller, Nelson Yokomizo

papers.title: A hierarchy of physics-embedded neural operators for structural dynamic surrogate modelingA hierarchy of physics-embedded neural operators for structural dynamic surrogate modeling
papers.abstract: Structural-response surrogates must capture moving resonances, phase changes, and unequal-amplitude transfer channels during optimization or health-state changes. Physics-embedded learning seeks FEA-level accuracy at lower cost by embedding physics in inputs, forward passes, losses, and backpropagation. We propose Modal Rational (MR), mapping structural features to modal quantities for analytical frequency-response reconstruction. The Physics-Guided Modal Operator Network (PGMON) adds bounded frequency, damping, and residual-flexibility corrections. Modal Operator with Structural GELU and Anchored-SIREN Correction (MOSAIC) denotes the bounded spectral-discrepancy framework used here; MOSAIC-MR and MOSAIC-PGMON add such discrepancies. They support finite-dimensional maps and physical decoders for future neural operators; evidence is fixed-topology, not a completed operator comparison. Two 20,000-design populations are studied: an 80 m steel truss tower with variable member areas and attached masses, and a tapered shell beam with ten variable station masses. Archived tests cover ten designs and seven acceleration histories per structure; they are benchmarks, not seismic-design assessments. With 5% reference modal damping, MR, PGMON, and MOSAIC give mean displacement-history errors of 0.73-0.76% for the tower and 0.029-0.116% for the beam, against declared band-limited modal references. Supplied modal frequencies are distinguished from design-only use; unequal parameter counts and training settings are explicit. Error analysis separates learned modal discrepancies, truncation, and excitation weighting, explaining acceleration and difficult-tower limits and risks of blind use. Results support physically structured prediction but limit claims about generalization, computational savings, and added corrections. Next is developing and validating neural operators around these architectures.
authors: Amir Ansrollahi, Mehmet Sefa Orak

papers.title: Quantum Noise Engineering in Advanced LIGO
papers.abstract: Advanced LIGO is a gravitational-wave detector with extreme sensitivity, operating close to the quantum limits of optical measurement. The quantum noise in this system arises from vacuum fluctuations entering the interferometer readout port: phase-like fluctuations produce measurement imprecision, while amplitude-like fluctuations drive radiation-pressure back-action. In this review, we present an intuitive description in terms of complex fields and quadratures, and follow squeezed vacuum from its generation, through its interaction with the filter cavity and propagation through the interferometer, to the readout. We discuss how frequency-independent and frequency-dependent squeezing engineer quantum noise, and how correlations between optical quadratures map onto correlations between measurement imprecision and back-action. We conclude that LIGO is both a gravitational-wave observatory and a kilometre-scale platform for quantum measurement science.
authors: Beg\"um Kabag\"oz

papers.title: Particle-loss error correction using $2^l$-step states generated via particle-number-resolving measurement schemes
papers.abstract: We present an iterative scheme for generating finite superpositions of Fock states whose photon numbers differ by $2^l$ ($2^l$-step states). We derive an upper bound on the probability of generating such states. Based on the proposed class of states, we construct several bosonic encodings and compare their performance in correcting particle-loss errors. Our results identify the most efficient encoding, which achieves a higher channel fidelity than previously studied bosonic encodings.
authors: S. B. Korolev, E. A. Nesterova

papers.title: Field-aligned measurement removes the anisotropy barrier of sample-based quantum subspace solvers for magnetized-plasma heat conduction
papers.abstract: Sample-based quantum subspace methods construct a small subspace from measured basis states and solve the target problem classically within it. We study these methods for heat conduction in magnetized plasmas, where the anisotropy $\chi_\parallel/\chi_\perp$ reaches $10^8$ to $10^{10}$. We prove two results for the energy-norm Galerkin solution. First, if the measurement basis is aligned with the flux surfaces and the subspace contains the poloidal-mode-zero block, the error is bounded by $\|r_0\|_{L^+}(\chi_\parallel-\chi_\perp)^{-1/2}$, where the numerator does not depend on $\chi_\parallel$. The bound is sharp, so the accuracy improves as the anisotropy grows. Second, in the computational basis, a subspace that misses a single node of a flux surface suppresses the flux-function component there as $\chi_\parallel^{-1/2}$, which gives an error floor when the limiting solution is nonzero on that surface. We verify both results on a shaped cross-section and on a KSTAR-like Miller equilibrium with ten qubits. At $\chi_\parallel/\chi_\perp=10^9$, the computational basis gives an error of order unity for every shot budget, whereas a quantum Fourier transform on the poloidal register gives $1.3\times10^{-5}$. The same barrier limits sample-based quantum diagonalization. The aligned measurement needs no time evolution, so the circuit is only state preparation and a five-qubit quantum Fourier transform. On a ten-qubit superconducting processor, the aligned basis gives a median error of $7.0\times10^{-6}$ with 768 shots, whereas the computational basis gives errors above 0.94 up to $1.2\times10^4$ shots. A trapped-ion processor shows the same behavior.
authors: Doyeol (David), Ahn (Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, University of Seoul, Dongdaemun-gu, Seoul, Republic of Korea, Singularity Quantum Inc., Newport Beach, California, USA)

papers.title: Nonequilibrium Spin-Glass Order in a Long-Range Quantum Ising Glass and Its Sensitivity to Noise
papers.abstract: We study spin-glass order after a transverse-field quench in a long-range quantum Ising glass. The diagonal-ensemble Edwards-Anderson order coincides at the no-quench and zero-field endpoints, yet in between cold shells overshoot it and hot shells undershoot it. This stems from a competition in correlation space between the rigidity of populated eigenstates and the spread of their pair patterns. Under weak longitudinal dephasing the zero-field endpoint is exactly pinned while the characteristic finite-quench response fades, giving a self-referenced noise probe for quantum spin simulators.
authors: Giuseppe D'Auria, Alessandro Silva

papers.title: The lattice Boltzmann machine
papers.abstract: The lattice Boltzmann (LB) method is widely regarded as a very flexible and efficient solver for a broad class of transport phenomena in fluids, soft matter and related fields. In this paper, we posit that such flexibility is a direct result of its generative nature as a rule-driven information-processing machine. Its update, a relaxation toward a local target followed by a shift along the lattice, belongs to the same class of iterated relaxation dynamics as residual networks and transformers, with the difference that in LB the operators are fixed by conservation and symmetry rather than learned from data. We show that three properties of this update are sufficient to promote the emergence of closed macroscopic laws from the underlying iteration process, the physical content of the target deciding the specific law in question. A machine whose target is drawn at random generates the transport law predicted from its moments. A network given the same three properties on a graph, where there is no lattice, is trained on a traffic process and generates a conservation law of its own. The mechanism has a precise limit, where the damping of the non-conserved modes fails, and on the lattice the macroscopic law gives no warning of it. In this reading, LB is a lattice Boltzmann machine whose informing rules are supplied by physics rather than by training. Its three properties then state what a new ingredient should preserve when it enters an LB model, whether it comes from physics or from data.
authors: Hua-Dong Yao, Sauro Succi

papers.title: Dithered Belief Propagation for Real-Time Quantum Memory Decoding
papers.abstract: We introduce dithered belief-propagation decoding for circuit-level quantum memory to mitigate the oscillations and trapping behavior that limit standard belief-propagation (BP) decoders for qLDPC codes. Our approach combines a quantum-adapted sign-flip mechanism with chained randomized prior perturbation. Evaluated under circuit-level noise on the distance-11 rotated surface code and the distance-12 bivariate-bicycle code, the proposed dithered decoder significantly outperforms BP and BP+OSD+CS-10. The proposed decoder achieves accuracy comparable to or better than state-of-the-art Relay-BP, especially at higher physical error rates, while trading a moderate increase in additions for about 98% fewer multiplications on average and eliminating node-level RNGs. These results suggest that dithering is a promising approach toward real-time decoding of quantum memories.
authors: Zhengyu Cai, Mohamad Ali Jarkas, Bokun Zhao, Warren J. Gross

papers.title: Improving Gravitationally Induced Entanglement in Interferometric Configurations
papers.abstract: Proposals to detect gravitationally induced entanglement between massive particles offer a promising pathway toward probing the quantum nature of gravity. We perform a systematic geometric optimization and comparative analysis of Stern--Gerlach (SG) and Mach--Zehnder (MZ) matter-wave interferometers for this purpose, deriving exact analytical expressions for the gravitational phase of each configuration. Our first key result is that geometric optimization is indispensable. For commonly assumed experimental parameters, neglecting the optimization of geometric ratios can suppress the accumulated phase, and hence the detectability of entanglement, by up to several orders of magnitude. Second, we provide a complete comparative analysis of two SG orientations (linear and parallel) and three MZ orientations (translation-symmetric, mirror-symmetric, and parallel-arms). The parallel-arms SG and MZ configurations tend to yield the largest phase accumulations and are nearly equivalent in performance, whereas the translation-symmetric MZ setup exhibits destructive-interference nulls that act as blind operating points where detection becomes ineffective. These observations highlight the importance of geometry-aware design. A Monte Carlo error analysis of realistic fabrication tolerances indicates that the parallel-arms configurations are generally more robust, maintaining low relative phase uncertainty over broad parameter intervals. Furthermore, an evaluation of Bell violations assesses the feasibility and signal-to-noise ratio of each configuration. Our results identify geometric optimization, particularly through parallel-arms designs, as an important consideration for near-term experiments targeting gravitationally induced entanglement.
authors: Alireza Maleki

papers.title: Scalable Transpilation for Overcoming Restricted Connectivity in Distributed Superconducting Quantum Architectures
papers.abstract: Distributed Quantum Computing (DQC) offers a promising pathway to scale superconducting quantum hardware, but restricted inter- and intra-module connectivity creates a major transpilation bottleneck. Current DQC transpilation methods often assume idealized hardware connectivity, ignore subsequent intra-module routing, or suffer from substantial computational overheads that limit their applicability at scale. To address this, we introduce a scalable transpilation method tailored for the restricted connectivity of distributed superconducting quantum architectures. Specifically, our quantum interaction graph (QIG) approach couples a graph-partitioning mapping step with a fast SABRE-inspired routing heuristic. On a 48-qubit (3 QPUs $\times$ 16 qubits) architecture with all-to-all inter-core connectivity, our method reduces average aggregated costs by up to 24.72% (unstructured) and 24.01% (structured), while delivering >250$\times$ speed-ups for structured workloads compared to the state-of-the-art DMapS algorithm. On the 399-qubit (3$\times$133) IBM Flamingo, where DMapS times out on dense circuits, our approach maintains practical runtimes. Against a DQC-adapted SABRE baseline, it reduces structured circuit routing costs by up to 51.94% (all-to-all inter-core topology) and 51.96% (restricted line topology). Ultimately, this work delivers a practical transpilation method for DQC at scale.
authors: Afonso Azenha, Ilia Polian, Sebastian Brandhofer

papers.title: On a Dual Heterotic Kodaira-Spencer Theory
papers.abstract: We consider a dual version of heterotic Kodaira-Spencer theory on a Calabi-Yau three-fold $X$ with background fluxes, related to the type I BCOV theory of Costello-Li. We implement the Green-Schwarz mechanism of Costello-Li, where the Beltrami differential plays the role of the Green-Schwarz field. On a compact Calabi-Yau three-fold with background gauge fluxes $F$, where $\mathrm{tr}(F^2)$ is trivial in cohomology, retaining gauge anomalies only and leaving gravitational anomalies to future work, we incorporate the Costello-Li Green-Schwarz mechanism into the classical deformation complex. This gives a theory governed by a nilpotent operator $\bar D$ on $Q=T^{1,0}X\oplus\operatorname{End}(V)\oplus T^{*1,0}X$, whose extension maps carry holomorphic derivatives, so that $(Q,\bar D)$ is not a holomorphic bundle. Using diagonal $\bar\partial^\dagger$-gauge, the one-loop gauge anomaly cancels, assuming that the extension maps of $\bar D$ do not modify it, which we argue is plausible. Introducing an auxiliary $(0,2)$-form, we construct a cubic interacting theory whose gauge symmetries are governed by an $L_3$ algebra. On compact Calabi-Yau three-folds, and for sufficiently small fields, we show that the equation of motion is equivalent to the Maurer-Cartan equation, together with a divergence-free constraint on the Beltrami differential. Finally we trivialise $\bar D$ locally to the Dolbeault operator. The (non-tensorial) transition maps glue into a quasi-holomorphic extension sheaf $\widetilde{\mathscr{Q}}$, for which we prove a Dolbeault theorem, $H^{0,q}_{\bar D}(Q)\cong\check H^q(\widetilde{\mathscr{Q}})$.
authors: Siddhartha Mangamuri, Eirik Eik Svanes, Anuthi Tiwary

papers.title: In light of the Henneaux-Teitelboim action
papers.abstract: We construct an action similar to the Henneaux-Teitelboim action on a six dimensional Lorentzian manifold where the time direction is chosen to be lightlike and generated by a conformal lightlike Killing vector $U$. We show that such an action exists only if there is another commuting light-like conformal Killing vector $V$ with properties that can be realized by the Dirac currents of two conformal Killing spinors. We extend the action to the $(1,0)$ supersymmetric tensor multiplet.
authors: Andreas Gustavsson

papers.title: Instantons from geometry in M2-brane sphere partition functions
papers.abstract: Can the geometry transverse to M2-branes capture effects that are exponentially small in their three-sphere ($S^3$) partition function? We investigate this question by extending beyond constant maps the proposal that M2-brane observables are encoded by equivariant topological strings on the transverse Calabi-Yau fourfold (CY$_4$). Our central object is the disk partition function of the CY$_4$ gauged linear sigma model, a quantum generalization of the equivariant volume. After a Gamma-function normalization and a Mellin transform, it reproduces the complete leading WKB grand potential in the examples admitting a suitable Fermi-gas description, including the R-charge and mass deformations compatible with that description. In particular, the transform recovers membrane-instanton series even for $\mathbb{C}^4$, which has no compact curves. For resolved CY$_4$ cones with compact curves, the match requires a quantum refinement of the classical mesonic constraint. We establish the exact equalities of the corresponding dressed disk partition functions with the classical spectral traces for ABJM, ADHM and a representative set of flavored M2-brane quiver theories. Away from the deformation loci where this match can be established, the same construction yields geometric predictions for the membrane-instanton sector that remain to be tested.
authors: Kiril Hristov, Ali Mert Yetkin

papers.title: Thermally-driven quantum reservoir computing
papers.abstract: Heat generation limits computation, classical and quantum, from single logic gates to entire data centers. However, an in principle limiting physical factor can sometimes be turned into a resource. In reservoir computing, energy dissipation is what gives a reservoir its fading memory. Here, we introduce a paradigm where the data injection itself is encoded on the time-dependent temperature of a thermal bath. We derive an exact expression for the nonlinear response of any fixed readout, and prove a rigorous memory-nonlinearity trade-off which turns out to be a structural necessity, rather than a tunable dynamical regime, since the same coupling that injects data also enforces equilibration. We illustrate both results with a driven qubit, using a single free parameter, and with a pair of coupled qubits, where the breaking of a discrete symmetry opens a fifteen-dimensional space to a single observable, yet that observable alone recovers just over half of it. This refutes the misconception that large Hilbert spaces guarantee computational power. Our results relocate the memory-nonlinearity trade-off from the reservoir's dynamics to its measurement channel, pointing to observable choice and bath engineering (instead of Hamiltonian control) as the physical levers for a thermally-native quantum reservoir computer.
authors: Thiago Werlang, Daniel Valente

papers.title: On the critical value of void percolation in high dimensions
papers.abstract: In the random Lorentz gas, a point tracer moves through spherical obstacles of (reduced) density $\Phi$ centered on a Poisson point process in $d$-dimensional space, $\mathbb{R}^d$, and becomes localized once the vacant space stops percolating, at $\Phi_{\rm p}(d)$. The dimensional scaling of this void percolation threshold has remained elusive. Prior bounds, conjectural ones included, ranged from $\Omega(1)$ to $O(d\ln d)$, leaving even the scaling undetermined. We here prove that $\Phi_{\rm p}(d)=\Theta(d)$, and in particular that $\tfrac12\,d \le \Phi_{\rm p}(d) \le 5\,d$ for all sufficiently large $d$. The upper bound counts hierarchical families of escape waypoints called tree embeddings; the lower bound is via a weighted second-moment estimate on an explicit ensemble of ballistic escape routes. A linear scaling of $\Phi_{\rm p}(d)$ excludes the $d\ln d$ growth suggested by analogy with other systems in the random first-order transition universality class and is consistent with the numerical estimate $\Phi_{\rm p}/d \to 3.40(5)$. Because the mean-field dynamical transition is likewise linear, $\Phi_{\rm d}\simeq 2.40\,d$, our result fixes the activated window $[\Phi_{\rm d},\Phi_{\rm p}]$ as a bounded---rather than diverging---correction to mean-field dynamical arrest in sufficiently high $d$.
authors: Patrick Charbonneau, Marcus Michelen

papers.title: Bearing, heading and the perceptual geometry of collective motion
papers.abstract: Traditional models of collective motion commonly assume that animals turn to match their neighbours' directions of travel. In the harmonic theory, decisions follow from a neural representation of direction, and a neighbour enters only as a stimulus at a bearing, the direction in which it lies. Here we show that a neighbour's spatial extent allows its orientation to enter through projection geometry alone, and the theory generates a matrix of coupling coefficients indexed by the neighbour's bearing and aspect. Responses to bearing alone form one edge of this matrix, and classical heading matching is a special case on its diagonal, one ray through a two-parameter family. Independently, an animal that responds only to neighbour position, perceived with a delay, acquires an alignment coefficient set by the slope of its distance-weighted attraction profile, so that it can align, anti-align or reverse sign. Alignment need not be a rule to be measured. In schooling fish and walking pigeons with body orientation measured independently of travel, social responses are recovered, including bearing responses in the fish. Heading excess depends on how turning is measured, appearing in the fish with forward but not centred responses and remaining unresolved in pigeons. Controls show why neither outcome identifies a direct alignment rule. In fish recordings with motion-assigned body polarity, heading-dependent structure departs from Vicsek form and fails the coefficient test for a common angular potential. Whether animals align thereby becomes a measurable question, with geometric, perceptual and behavioural origins that can be distinguished.
authors: Mohammad Salahshour

papers.title: Upper and lower bounds for few-copy Gaussian tomography, and the absence of a fermionic warm regime
papers.abstract: Chen, Mele, Mele and Preskill proved a crossover for bosonic Gaussian tomography: cold states need $\Theta(m^3/\epsilon^2)$ copies under single-copy or few-copy measurements, warm ones $\Theta(m^2/\epsilon^2)$. The author proved $\Omega(m^3/\epsilon^2)$ for adaptive single-copy tomography of mixed fermionic Gaussian states. This note shows the crossover has no fermionic counterpart and extends the fermionic bound to blocks of $k$ copies. There is no warm regime: on the quadratic Gibbs balls $\beta\|h\|_F\le\beta_0$ of unknown Hamiltonian $h$, the single-copy rate is $\Theta(m^3/\epsilon^2)$ for every fixed $\beta_0>0$, at accuracies that resolve the ball, with a lower-bound constant independent of $\beta_0$. At the maximally mixed state a replicated-parameter Fisher budget gives $N>m^3/(8{,}553{,}600\,k\,\epsilon^2)$ for blocks of at most $k$ copies and all $\epsilon\le1/3600$; an exact formula for the maximal block Fisher information, via spinor tensor powers of $\mathfrak{so}(2m)$, shows that the budget $mt^2$ behind it is asymptotically attained for every fixed block size; whether $1/k$ is the true rate is open. Near the vacuum, block protocols need $\Omega(m^3/(\epsilon^2\min\{\sqrt k,m\}))$ copies, with no logarithm, via an exterior-power embedding of qudit tomography; parity superselection changes no rate, and number superselection costs nothing on number-conserving inputs. The embedding also carries upper bounds: a particle-number measurement followed by the $k$-copy qudit protocol of Nayak and Zhou attains the lower bound for every $k$ on number-conserving fermionic Gaussian states with bounded fugacity trace and on passive bosonic Gaussian states with bounded photon number, and a heterodyne stage that undoes displacement and squeezing extends this to all cold bosonic Gaussian states. This closes their $k$-entangled gap on the cold class; intermediate temperatures remain open.
authors: Ron Rubin

papers.title: Unifying First-Order Coherence, Concurrence, and Bell Correlations in Three-Flavor Neutrino Oscillations
papers.abstract: Neutrino oscillations provide a natural setting for investigating the quantum character of flavor conversion and the distribution of quantum resources over macroscopic distances. Here, we study exact relations among purity-based first-order coherence, pairwise concurrence, and the maximal Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt (CHSH) value in coherent three-flavor neutrino oscillations. By expressing the evolving neutrino as a three-qubit single-excitation state, we derive the generally mixed two-qubit reductions and show that the squared first-order coherence of each flavor mode and its two associated squared concurrences sum to unity. Furthermore, a closed two-branch relation is obtained, showing that the maximal CHSH value of any reduced pair is determined by its average first-order coherence and concurrence. The branch structure follows from the correlation-tensor spectrum and yields exact conditions for CHSH violation. For the vacuum parameters and propagation ranges considered, electron preparation gives weak CHSH violations in electroncontaining pairs, while muon preparation produces a dominant utau pair with substantially stronger concurrence and Bell correlations. The comparison also identifies the thirdflavor contribution responsible for the different locations of concurrence and CHSH maxima. These results clarify the distribution of quantum correlations during flavor evolution and provide a basis for extensions to coherent matter propagation and wave-packet-induced mixed states.
authors: Bingbing Li, Tao Wu, Jiadong Shi

papers.title: Quantum simulation of classical RCL circuits via complexification and Schr\"odingerization
papers.abstract: The decomplexification procedure establishes a mathematical equivalence between finite dimensional quantum dynamics and classical dynamics by mapping the complex quantum domain onto the real classical one. Its inverse process, complexification --- which lifts a classical dynamics to an equivalent quantum formulation --- is of great interest, particularly because it enables the quantum simulation of equations that are of classical relevance. In this way, one can prepare the solution of classical differential equations to be implemented using quantum computation tools. In the present work, we recall the decomplexification procedure and also discuss several distinct strategies for performing the complexification of classical equations, so as to obtain the corresponding quantum-equivalent dynamics.
authors: Huner Fanchiotti, Carlos A. Garc\'ia Canal, Miguel A. Mayosky, Alejandro L. Veiga, Armando P\'erez, Rafael G\'omez-Lurbe, Vicente Vento

papers.title: Background Effects on Thermal Free Energy in Conformal Field Theories
papers.abstract: We compute background corrections to the thermal free energy of free conformal field theories (CFTs) with a global abelian symmetry defined on a box with all sides infinitely long by turning on a flat gauge field in general dimensions. This result is applied to the U(N) maximally supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory, the ABJ(M) theory, and the free U(N) vector model in four, three, and two spacetime dimensions, respectively. In these examples, the thermal free energies monotonically increase as the background field does, and cross a zero within the valid range. We argue that the systems undergo a phase transition at the zero, where the effective degrees of freedom fall off similarly to the color-confinement one, and that it always occurs if the number of matter fields is greater than a critical value. We comment for this phase transition to circumvent the Mermin-Wagner-Coleman theorem in two spacetime dimensions.
authors: Shuichi Yokoyama, Ibuki Yoshida, Hiroki Yunoto

papers.title: Asymptotic advantage of quantum one-way and SMP communication for total functions
papers.abstract: We exhibit a total Boolean function on n input bits whose bounded-error quantum simultaneous-message (and hence one-way) communication complexity is in O(\sqrt n), whereas its randomised one-way (and hence simultaneous-message) communication complexity is in \Omega(n). The same function admits a classical simultaneous-message protocol of cost O(\sqrt n) when the players share O(\sqrt n) EPR pairs.
authors: Dmytro Gavinsky

papers.title: Frustration-freeness is decidable but unprovable
papers.abstract: The frustration-free property is valuable in quantum many-body systems, which states that its ground states simultaneously minimize all local interaction terms, even when these terms act on overlapping degrees of freedom. Prominent examples include the AKLT model and Kitaev's toric code model, which serve as paradigmatic models of symmetry-protected topological phases and topological order, respectively. A fundamental question is whether a given Hamiltonian is frustration-free for all system sizes. Here we establish two seemingly contradictory results concerning this decision problem. First, we prove that frustration-freeness is decidable for any fixed local Hilbert space dimension. Specifically, there exists a finite, Hamiltonian-independent system-size cutoff such that frustration-freeness at this cutoff size guarantees frustration-freeness at all system sizes. Second, on the other hand, we also show that there exists a frustration-free Hamiltonian whose frustration-freeness cannot be proved within the standard axioms of mathematics (ZFC). We reconcile these seemingly contradictory results by showing that the cutoff, although finite for each local Hilbert space dimension, is uncomputable as a function of that dimension. Our findings reveal an unexpected fundamental distinction between decidability and provability arising in quantum many-body physics.
authors: Naoto Shiraishi

papers.title: Fidelity Determines the Minimum Error of Quantum Recovery
papers.abstract: Even a recovery that maximizes worst-input entanglement fidelity can retain avoidable errors in subsequent measurements. Entanglement fidelity is the probability of passing a test of whether the state and its entanglement were preserved; infidelity is the probability of failing it. Operational error is the largest possible change in any measurement probability, quantified by the normalized diamond distance. For every finite-dimensional noise channel and fixed encoding, we prove that operational error and worst-input entanglement infidelity have the same minimum over all recovery operations. The proof constructs one final unitary (a reversible quantum operation) that makes any recovery's operational error no greater than its original worst-input entanglement infidelity. With a retained noise record, we determine the optimal error and characterize all optimal decoders subject to a Kraus-rank limit for each outcome. For a fixed decoded channel, a semidefinite program finds the optimal final unitary in the low-error regime. We characterize all optimal final corrections and show that, at a fixed error floor $0<\epsilon<1$, the operational optimizers' sensitivity to residual unitary errors of size $s$ is at worst of order $s^{4/3}$, while the canonical polar correction has quadratic sensitivity.
authors: Dario Picozzi

papers.title: Observable-Based Learning of Effective Entanglement Hamiltonians
papers.abstract: Determining the entanglement Hamiltonian (EH) of an interacting quantum many-body system remains a fundamental challenge beyond special analytically tractable cases. Here we develop an observable-matching framework for learning effective EHs, which we demonstrate using response estimates from quantum Monte Carlo. As applications of this framework, we first calibrate the overall prefactor of the lattice Bisognano--Wichmann (LBW) construction using equal-time correlations and then learn spatially resolved couplings beyond its prescribed profile, without assuming a specific functional form for their spatial dependence. Trained solely on local correlations, the learned EHs reproduce benchmarked von Neumann and second R\'enyi entropies in $1$D and second R\'enyi entropies in $2$D. For a strong-bond cut associated with special surface criticality at the $(2+1)$D $O(3)$ Wilson--Fisher critical point, free-form learning outperforms the calibrated LBW ansatz in predicting the second R\'enyi entropy and reveals spatially nonuniform coupling renormalizations. Importantly, the learned EH also provides access to the von Neumann entropy in this setting, revealing a negative subleading correction and extending previous R\'enyi entropy findings to the von Neumann case. Directly evaluating the von Neumann entropy in such $(2+1)$D interacting quantum many-body systems remains challenging for conventional numerical methods. These results establish observable-based learning as a route to constructing effective entanglement Hamiltonians beyond prescribed spatial profiles in higher-dimensional interacting systems.
authors: Siyi Yang, Yuzhi Liu, Yi-Ming Ding, Zheng Yan

papers.title: Operational Characterizations and Resource Structure of the Interactive Weight of Quantum Instruments
papers.abstract: Quantifying the interactivity of quantum instruments is fundamental to understanding their resource structure and operational capabilities. Here, we introduce the interactive weight of quantum instruments as a resource quantifier that measures the minimum fraction of an instrument that cannot be explained by non-interactive components. Through quantum-information tasks including quantum-state recovery, positive linear loss games, and environment-assisted input-blind extraction, we establish quantitative bounds on the interactive weight of quantum instruments and exact operational characterizations of its complementary quantity, the maximal non-interactive content. In particular, we extend environment-assisted input-blind extraction to the setting of restricted environmental access and develop a corresponding framework. Within the allowed-operations framework introduced by Hsieh et al., we establish fundamental resource-theoretic properties of the interactive weight of quantum instruments, including faithfulness, convexity, and monotonicity under deterministic allowed operations. Furthermore, we prove that the maximal non-interactive content satisfies exact multiplicativity under independent parallel composition, yielding necessary constraints on multicopy resource conversion and establishing the finite-copy maximal-weight distillation no-go result under deterministic allowed operations. These results establish a unified theoretical framework for the interactive weight of quantum instruments from the perspectives of resource quantification, operational interpretation, and resource conversion, providing systematic theoretical tools for the quantitative comparison and conversion of interactive quantum instruments.
authors: Yongxi He, Xin Hong, Yu Luo, Xiangzhen Zhou, Shenggang Ying

papers.title: Non-symmetric integral geometry: alternative reconstruction procedure with dual Radon transform
papers.abstract: In the note, we use the principles of non-symmetric integral geometry (non-integral geometry), related to the non-symmetric restricted integration measure, to extend the well-known relations traced from the Fourier slice theorem and the dual Radon transform. The proposed generalization is a very useful for the alternative restoration of the outset function. The latter impacts entirely on the image reconstruction process. The derived relations confirm the complexity of the inversion operator thanks for the symmetry breaking of integration measure.
authors: I. V. Anikin

papers.title: Spin-Exchange-Controlled Nonclassical Light in Cavity Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
papers.abstract: Controlling nonclassical light while maintaining a finite cavity response requires selective suppression of unwanted multiphoton excitation. We investigate a ring-cavity system containing two three-level emitters coupled by a coherent spin-exchange interaction, where electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) provides resonant access to a dark-state polariton. The exchange interaction shifts the polariton resonance while modifying the dressed two-photon excitation pathways. Strong photon antibunching emerges when the one-polariton resonance nearly coincides with a destructive-interference minimum of the second-photon transition amplitude. By jointly tuning the exchange interaction and control-field strength, pronounced photon blockade with a finite intracavity population can be sustained over an extended interaction range. We further show that the relative cavity-coupling phase redistributes optical coupling between symmetric and antisymmetric collective channels with opposite exchange shifts, allowing the photon statistics to switch between antibunching and bunching at fixed exchange strength. This mechanism provides a possible route to tunable nonclassical-light sources based on coherent control of collective excitation pathways.
authors: Jing Tang, Junyu Su, Jie Chen, Ziyang Li, Yuangang Deng

papers.title: Certifying the Rydberg-exposure limit of a globally driven controlled-Z gate
papers.abstract: Rydberg excitation enables entangling gates in neutral-atom quantum processors but also exposes them to spontaneous decay. Whether this exposure can be made arbitrarily small through pulse shaping and longer gate times has remained unresolved. We show that an exact controlled-$Z$ gate driven by a single global laser has an irreducible Rydberg-exposure cost in the perfect-blockade regime. The product of the maximum Rabi frequency $\Omega_{\max}$ and the average time $T_R$ spent in the Rydberg state is bounded below by $2.9312$, independent of pulse shape and duration. We derive this bound using a sum-of-squares certificate, strengthened by constraints imposed by the shared drive. Using interval arithmetic, we also certify the existence of an exact gate pulse with $\Omega_{max} T_R<2.9359$. The unrounded bounds differ by less than $0.16\%$. The bound identifies a fundamental cost of shared-drive entangling dynamics and establishes a benchmark against which future gate-control strategies can be assessed.
authors: Yusheng Zhao, Han Wang, Mingrui Jing, Zhongyi Ni, Xin Wang, Jie Wang, Jinguo Liu

papers.title: Improved method for extracting low-energy expansion from OPE in mass-gapped theories
papers.abstract: Recently, Takaura proposed a new method for extracting the first nonzero coefficient of the low-energy expansion of an observable from its operator product expansion (OPE) in asymptotically free theories with a mass gap and a single threshold. The method uses a weight function to suppress the contribution of the ``duality-violation'' (DV) term that arises when relating the OPE to the low-energy expansion. We extend this method to low-energy expansion coefficients at arbitrary orders. We present two approaches: Method I uses weight functions that isolate the coefficients of low-energy expansion from the OPE. Method II subtracts the DV contribution from the OPE before the extraction. Applying these methods to the two-dimensional large-$N$ $O(N)$ nonlinear sigma model, we find that both methods successfully reconstruct higher-order low-energy expansion coefficients.
authors: Hajime Furuta, Yukinari Sumino

papers.title: $1/N$ corrections to $\langle TJJ\rangle$ and $\langle TTT\rangle$ in the critical $O(N)$ vector and Gross--Neveu--Yukawa models
papers.abstract: We compute the subleading corrections in the $1/N$ expansion of the three-point functions $\langle TJJ\rangle$ and $\langle TTT\rangle$ in the three-dimensional critical $O(N)$ vector and Gross--Neveu--Yukawa models. We determine the coefficients of the two parity-even conformal structures and the corresponding conformal collider parameters. The calculation uses an expansion of momentum-space Feynman diagrams in a soft external momentum, together with the contact terms required by background gauge and metric sources. The sums of the structure coefficients reproduce the known current and stress-tensor two-point normalizations. We also compute these coefficients independently using the metric and mixed metric--gauge derivatives of the sphere free energy. Extrapolating the large $N$ results to the $O(2)$ vector model yields reasonably good agreement with recent numerical bootstrap bounds. At $N=2$, our $\gamma$ and $t_4$ predictions lie within the joint bootstrap region under weaker spectral assumptions; their deviations from the more restrictive interval midpoints are only $3.28\%$ and $4.44\%$, respectively. We discuss the implications for energy flux, high-frequency conductivity, and shear response near quantum criticality.
authors: Yongwei Guo, Zhijin Li

papers.title: Extensions of the Haldane gap proof: higher dimensions, near degeneracy, fermions and tensor-network states
papers.abstract: A recent remarkable paper by OpenAI showed that the spin-one Heisenberg chain with periodic boundary conditions has a spectral gap in the thermodynamic limit.
